The western half of the Roman Empire when it had its own emperor, above all from 395 to 476. The map shows it in 400, still holding Italy, Gaul, Spain, Britain and North Africa, and keeps the label in 500, when its lands were already Germanic kingdoms.

When Theodosius I died in 395, his young sons split the empire, and Honorius took the west, ruling from Milan and then Ravenna. Real power lay with generals such as Stilicho and later Aetius. Rome let go of Britain around 410, the end of Roman rule in Britain, and in the same year the Visigoths carried out the sack of Rome. The Vandals crossed to Africa and took Carthage in 439, cutting off the richest province. Aetius stopped Attila at the Catalaunian Plains in 451, but in 455 the Vandals sacked Rome again.

The last emperors were puppets of barbarian generals. In 476 Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople. The Eastern Roman Empire lasted almost a thousand years longer.
